*I’d block shipment on one correctness issue.*

*P1 — Renewal dates use the wrong month’s length* — `src/schedule.js:6–7`

The day is clamped against the *source* month, then used to construct a date in the *next* month. This breaks the documented month-end behavior:

| From | Anchor | Expected | Actual |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Jan 31, 2026 | 31 | Feb 28 | Mar 3 |
| Feb 28, 2026 | 31 | Mar 31 | Mar 28 |
| Apr 30, 2026 | 31 | May 31 | May 30 |

When the target month is shorter, JavaScript rolls the invalid date into the following month, skipping a renewal month. When it’s longer, the renewal lands before the anchor.

Clamp against the *target month’s* length instead. Add regression tests for January → February, February → March (including leap years), and 30-day → 31-day transitions.

*Validation:* All 5 existing tests pass, but an additional in-memory sweep of anchors 1–31 across every month in 2026–2028 found 40 incorrect dates out of 1,116 cases.

Reviewed `billing-anniversary` at `f73b00d` against `main` at `7f89e48`. No files changed.
